blocks.text: 如今，由42位州总检察长组成的联盟正在介入Character.ai的破产程序，试图阻止这家聊天机器人制造商出售敏感用户数据，其中包含数百万用户的私人对话。

inlines.text: 如今，由42位州总检察长组成的联盟正在介入Character.ai的破产程序，试图阻止这家聊天机器人制造商出售敏感用户数据，其中包含数百万用户的私人对话。

blocks.text: 参与此事的各位总检察长分别发布了各自的新闻稿，称Character.ai的数据集包含超过2100万个美国账户的聊天记录，其中超过210万个账户属于未成年人。声明还称，此次出售还将涉及IP地址等其他个人数据。

blocks.text: 声明还指出，Character.ai已于10月申请第11章破产保护，此前曾向消费者承诺不会出售其个人信息。（在一篇博客文章中，Character.ai向用户保证，其信息仍将受到隐私政策的保护。）

blocks.text: 目前只披露了一个匿名竞标者：Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC（简称Smirks），该公司于2026年11月13日在特拉华州注册成立。据加州总检察长Rob Bonta指出，次日，Character.ai将其选为定于12月1日举行的拍卖的底价。目前尚不清楚买家的聊天记录处置计划。

blocks.text: 总检察长们反对此次出售，理由是用户得不到任何保护——他们说，无论谁买下这些数据，都可以为所欲为，包括在不披露的情况下转售数据。买家也不必遵守Character.ai的隐私政策。此外，总检察长们还声称，关于出售后可能出现的任何安全或法律问题，Character.ai向法院提供的信息不如向竞标者提供的信息充分。

blocks.text: 此外，包括加州、科罗拉多州、纽约州和康涅狄格州在内的一些州已颁布聊天机器人安全立法，将于2027年1月1日生效，如果此次出售获批，可能会引发更多违规行为。

blocks.text: Bonta在一份声明中表示：“Character.AI向消费者承诺不会出售他们的数据。这种行为根据联邦法律和加州法律均属违法，破产不应被用来规避这些消费者保护措施。”

inlines.text: 康涅狄格州总检察长William Tong也批评了Character.ai的商业模式。

blocks.text: “他们的聊天机器人把脆弱的青少年推入了情绪波动和性不当对话的兔子洞，”Tong说。“他们鲁莽的不当行为和破碎的商业模式把公司拖入了深渊。现在他们想滥用破产程序，去做他们曾承诺不会做的事——把那些私人聊天记录和个人详细信息拍卖给一个来路不明的买家。”

blocks.text: Tong补充道：“我们曾反对迪士尼的出售，现在我们呼吁破产法院也拒绝这笔出售，因为这不过是又一个用来规避法律责任和消费者保护的幌子。”

blocks.text: 反对迪士尼这笔交易的一方，是由各州总检察长组成的联盟牵头，成员构成与前者类似但并不完全相同。他们反对的是一项拟议中的2000万美元授权协议，该协议将让迪士尼获得Character.ai的知识产权，但不包括用户的聊天记录。这笔交易尚未获得法院最终批准。（迪士尼还同意聘用Character.ai剩余的大部分员工。）

blocks.text: What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

inlines.text: What happens to your private conversations when an
AI company goes bankrupt
? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

blocks.text: Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

inlines.text: Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

blocks.text: The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.

, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.

blocks.text: Character.ai, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October, previously told consumers that their personal information would not be sold, the statements also noted. (In a blog post, Character.ai assured its users that their information would still be protected under its privacy policy.)

blocks.text: Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats.

blocks.text: The AGs are opposing this sale on the grounds that there are no protections for users — whoever buys the data can do as they like, including reselling the data without disclosure, they said. Buyers also won’t have to honor Character.ai’s privacy policy. Plus, Character.ai hasn’t provided the court with as much information as the bidders have been given about any potential safety or legal issues following the sale, the AGs claim.

blocks.text: In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

blocks.text: “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.

blocks.text: Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

inlines.text: Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

blocks.text: “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”

blocks.text: Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”

blocks.text: The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.)
